title: Главные блюда для Артёма  (Main Courses for Artyom)

segments.t: Having figured out that Artyom is Eleonora's secret favorite, Chef Barinov sets a culinary trap. He announces that Eleonora has a VIP dinner in two hours and assigns Artyom to cook all the main courses himself so her guests will taste his awful cooking.
Пришло время поработать!
У хозяйки через пару часов важная встреча.
Сеня, Федя, берёте закуски.
Луи, с тебя десерт.
Хорошо, шеф. А горячее кто?
А все главные блюда готовит Артём!
Она обещала зайти на кухню с проверкой.
Так что придётся готовить лично.
Но ты не волнуйся, я буду всё пробовать и подсказывать.
Хорошо, шеф.
Я верю в тебя!
Это будет интересно.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Пришло время поработать!
'The time has come to do some work!' Notice how Russian expresses 'to come' and 'to work' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
У хозяйки через пару часов важная встреча.
'In a couple of hours the owner has an important meeting.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'at' and 'landlady' in a few short words.
Сеня, Федя, берёте закуски.
'Senya, Fedya, you take the appetizers.' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'Senya', while 'appetizers' completes the thought.
Луи, с тебя десерт.
'Louis, dessert is on you.' Chef Barinov addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'dessert'. Senya answers right away.
Хорошо, шеф. А горячее кто?
'Alright, chef. And who has the hot entrees?' Senya brings out the contrast between 'well' and 'proper name' in a few short words.
А все главные блюда готовит Артём!
'And Artyom is cooking all the main courses!' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'Artyom' without extra filler words.
Она обещала зайти на кухню с проверкой.
'She promised to stop by the kitchen for an inspection.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'she' and finishing on 'check'.
Так что придётся готовить лично.
'So you will have to cook personally.' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'so', while 'personally' completes the thought.
Но ты не волнуйся, я буду всё пробовать и подсказывать.
'But do not worry, I will taste everything and coach you.' The grammar packs 'but' and 'to prompt' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Хорошо, шеф.
'Alright, chef.' Denis brings out the contrast between 'well' and 'proper name' in a few short words. Chef Barinov answers right away.
Я верю в тебя!
'I believe in you!' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'you' in spoken Russian.
Это будет интересно.
'This is going to be interesting.' The grammar packs 'this' and 'interesting' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
